summary: Astronaut Health Monitor is a web app that helps astronauts check their own health on space missions, even when a doctor is far away. The astronaut enters 13 readings about their body, habitat and sleep. The software grades each one green, yellow, orange or red using limits from NASA documents, gives a health score from 0 to 100, and explains in plain words what to do next. It answers the challenge "Create Health Monitoring Software for Astronauts on Space Missions" with NASA's recommended features: an interactive body map, color-coded status, time charts, five mission environments, routine reminders, a daily game and step-by-step measuring guides. It also loads real ISS radiation data from NASA's RadLab. Each astronaut's data is private. It matters because crews far from Earth must act first, and they need clear help, not raw numbers.
details:
WHAT IT DOES: The astronaut enters 13 health indicators in three groups: body vitals (heart rate, blood pressure, blood oxygen, temperature), habitat and radiation (cabin CO2, cabin pressure, radiation), and sleep and wellbeing. Each indicator is graded Nominal, Advisory, Warning or Critical. The software creates a 0-100 health score and a list of actions. Critical findings say to contact the Flight Surgeon.

HOW IT WORKS: A React website talks to a Node.js and Express server. The server checks every value, saves each reading in a MySQL database, and runs a rule-based evaluation engine (not machine learning). Each astronaut sees only their own data. Real NASA data: a panel loads live ISS radiation measurements from NASA OSDR RadLab and shows them next to the astronaut's own reading. The astronaut can download a health report as a PDF or an image, and gets alert and weekly reminder emails.

FEATURES (from NASA's design recommendations): interactive body map, color-coded status, time-series charts, five mission environments (station, spacecraft, rover, Moon, Mars), routine check reminders, a gamified daily challenge, and step-by-step "how to measure" guidance for people who are not doctors.

IMPACT: faster understanding of health without a doctor, fewer missed checks, and a calm interface under stress.

TOOLS: React, Tailwind CSS, Node.js, Express, MySQL, PDFKit, Nodemailer.

IMPORTANT: all astronaut readings are simulated. This is a prototype and not medical advice. To try the app, create a free account with any email (no code needed).

AI: AI (Claude) helped write and review the code, the interface and the slides. The code is acknowledged as AI-assisted in the repository README.
